Exclusion de garantie

A specific condition or circumstance listed in an insurance policy for which benefits will not be paid, limiting the insurer’s liability.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Exclusion de garantie?

In this glossary, Exclusion de garantie refers to: A specific condition or circumstance listed in an insurance policy for which benefits will not be paid, limiting the insurer’s liability.

How is Exclusion de garantie used in finance?

In finance communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Les exclusions de garantie doivent être clairement énoncées dans le contrat afin que l’assuré comprenne les limites de sa couverture."

Why does Exclusion de garantie matter in finance?

Exclusion de garantie matters because it supports clear communication in Insurance contexts for Financial Analysts, Bankers, and Traders. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as CFA, ACCA, and FRM.
